Why do curved follicles require specialized punch technique and experience?

Afro-textured and tightly coiled hair curves beneath the skin surface rather than growing straight down, so a standard straight-hair punch angle can slice through the follicle root and reduce graft survival. Experienced surgical teams adjust punch diameter, depth control and extraction angle for each curl pattern to limit transection.

As the [International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery (ISHRS) notes on hair restoration in African-American patients](https://ishrs.org/hair-restoration-in-african-americans/), while the core surgical mechanics mirror other hair types, the pronounced curl under the dermis makes extraction more technically demanding. A clinic that handles mostly straight European or Middle Eastern hair may underestimate dermal thickness and curl radius. High transection rates waste limited donor supply and can leave patchy thinning at the back of the scalp, which is why verifying direct physician involvement matters.
What specific portfolio proof should Afro-textured hair patients request?

Request at least five unedited case studies of patients with your exact curl pattern (Type 3C to 4C) showing clear pre-op, Day 10 and 12-month post-op photographs of both the hairline and the donor zone. Consistent lighting, wet and dry shots and close-up fade views reveal far more than studio marketing clips.
Do not rely on three-month growth updates or heavily shadowed photos. Ask whether the same named surgeon who will lead your procedure performed the cases shown.

items: Matched hair type: Confirm the cases match your curl tightness, hair shaft calibre and skin tone.
Full 12-month maturity: Verify healed outcomes at 10 to 14 months rather than immediate post-op graft placement photos.
Donor-area transparency: Request short-fade or buzzed donor photos to check for visible hypopigmented dots or over-harvesting.
Natural hairline design: Look for age-appropriate, slightly irregular hairlines rather than overly sharp, artificial straight lines.

Named operator proof: Confirm in writing who performs the scoring, extraction and recipient site creation, in line with [ISHRS patient guidelines](https://ishrs.org/ishrs-guidelines-for-patients-seeking-hair-restoration-surgery/).

body.text: Does FUE vs DHI matter more for curly hair?

For Afro-textured hair, extraction skill matters more than whether grafts are implanted with forceps or a DHI implanter pen. Both FUE with pre-made incisions and DHI use the same follicular unit extraction step first, and tight curls can occasionally bend inside narrow implanter needles if the team lacks curly-hair experience.
Choosing between standard FUE and DHI is a clinical decision your surgeon should justify after examining your scalp in person.

What keloid or scarring screening should happen before travel?

Before booking flights, disclose any personal or family history of keloids, hypertrophic scars, acne keloidalis nuchae or traction alopecia to a qualified dermatologist at home and to your prospective surgical team. Pre-travel screening helps your doctors decide whether surgery is appropriate or whether a small test session is safer.

According to the [American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) overview on keloid scars](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/keloids-overview), keloids grow much larger than the original wound, and the [AAD diagnosis guide](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/keloids-treatment) notes that a board-certified dermatologist can evaluate suspicious scars clinically or via biopsy. If you have active scalp inflammation, central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (CCCA) or prior raised scarring, a responsible surgeon will pause or decline cosmetic grafting until a dermatologist confirms scalp stability. Remember that [ISHRS](https://ishrs.org/questions-ask-your-hair-doctor/) explicitly warns there is no such thing as "scarless" hair transplant surgery.

Once your medical team confirms suitability, plan your return-home care carefully using our [first 14 days after a hair transplant checklist](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/hair-transplant-first-14-days).

faq.q: Can Afro-textured hair achieve good density with fewer grafts?
faq.a: Tightly coiled hair often creates greater visual coverage per follicle than straight hair because of its curl volume, though exact graft numbers are always determined by your surgeon during an in-person donor assessment.

faq.q: Is FUT strip surgery better than FUE for curly hair?
faq.a: FUT can protect curved roots during microscopic dissection, but it leaves a linear scar that restricts short fade haircuts. Your surgeon will weigh donor density, curl tightness and your preferred hairstyle.

faq.q: Can women with traction alopecia get an Afro hair transplant in Türkiye?
faq.a: Some women with stable traction alopecia are candidates, provided active hair-pulling inflammation has stopped and a physician rules out scarring alopecias before surgery.

faq.q: How can I check if a Turkish clinic is officially authorized?
faq.a: Verify its International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate through the [Turkish Ministry of Health Health Tourism Department](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) and confirm the named surgeon's credentials directly.

faq.q: Should I shave my hair before flying to Istanbul?
faq.a: No. Keep your natural hair length until your face-to-face consultation so the surgeon can assess curl direction, donor density and existing scalp skin clearly.
